equivalents.note: The Tibetan reads helī as a woman: the Śabara takes stong pa'i mi mo, 'the woman of emptiness'.
The Tibetan renders bilasanti with sgeg, 'to sport amorously', and the comment has sgeg cing rol pa for vilasati krīḍati (cp.50.m3), so sgeg answers to vi-las and rol to krīḍ.
Transcribed sa wa ri, the form the Tibetan also uses for Śabarapāda and for the Śabarī, so it does not single out this term.
The verse has bzi ba, 'drunk', where the comment's word for Munidatta's pramatta is myos pa (cp.50.m6).
Here the Tibetan translates rather than transcribes: rngon pa, 'hunter'.
The Tibetan renders śabarāśabari as one phrase, rngon pa pho mo, 'hunter man and woman', so the Śabarī is only the mo of the pair; the comment has rngon pa mo (cp.50.m6).
Spelled sha wa ri pa here, against sa wa ri in 2b, 6b and 7b.
Where the Sanskrit has 'the three emptinesses beginning with light' (lokādi-), the Tibetan has de la bsnun pa la sogs pa, 'striking it and so on', so light (āloka) is not rendered.
A calque of karmāṅganā that reads aṅganā, 'woman', as aṅga, 'limb', with a possessive, 'the one with limbs of action', matching the verse's ma rung yan lag can for dundolī.
The comment cites the phrase as zla ba shar ba, 'the moon rising', putting the moon for johnā, 'moonlight'.

questions: bari (cp.50.1a): not matched. The Tibetan line has nam mkha' nam mkhar son pa, 'what has grown up to the sky', reading bāḍhī as 'grown' rather than 'field'; the term is already matched in cp.50.3a (ldum ra).

taila (cp.50.1a, cp.50.3a, cp.50.m5): not matched. The Tibetan has no separate word for tailā: in 3a tailā bāṛī is simply ldum ra, 'garden', in the m5 lemma ldum ra'i rtsa ba, and nothing in 1a answers to it. The comment's gsum pa, 'third', renders Munidatta's tṛtīya, not tailā.

sandhya-bhasa (cp.50.m2, cp.50.m7): not matched. In both places the Tibetan reads sandhyā as 'joining' or 'junction', not as twilight language (dgongs pa'i skad): de la sbyar zhing bsdus pa'i rigs pas (m2) and de mtshams bzhir (m7).
bhava (cp.50.m3): not matched. The Tibetan has bde ba chen po'i ngo bo stong pa nyid, with ngo bo, 'nature', apparently reading bhāve; there is no srid pa, 'existence'.
guru-vacana (cp.50.m4): not matched. The Tibetan has bla ma'i zhabs kyi drin gyis, 'by the kindness of the guru's feet', with zhabs, 'feet', where the Sanskrit has vacana, 'word'.

parsva (cp.50.m5): given only from cp.50.m4 (rtsa bar). For tṛtīyaśūnyapārśve the Tibetan has stong pa gsum pa la gnyen po, 'the antidote (or ally) to the third emptiness'; gnyen po does not plainly render 'side'. The m5 lemma ldum ra'i rtsa ba does have rtsa ba for the verse's pāsem̐ra.
anusamsa (cp.50.m6): not matched. The Tibetan segment opens kaM gu tsa na zhes pa ni bzhi pa skye ba med pa..., with no word for praise.
bed (cp.50.m6): not matched. The Tibetan has sems med par gyur nas nyal ba'o, 'became mindless and lay down', with nyal ba for supta and nothing for śayyā, 'bed'.
cancali (cp.50.m7): no answer. The comment cites the word as gtum mo, that is caṇḍālī, a different word; the term is already matched in cp.50.6a (smyug ma'i rib ma).
